audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) Both deciding quotations verified in copies we hold at the stated loci (Capidan p.96 on the page scan; Papahagi djvu text l.4713-4714). (2) The classification lexical rested on transcription conventions in a 1925 reference grammar and a 1902 glossary (inferential, as a check and B both flagged). (3) downloaded now: Narumov 2001 (Jazyki mira: Romanskie jazyki, p.675, open institutional scan) states explicitly that Megleno-Romanian stress is dynamic and free and may fall on any syllable, with final/antepenult/penult examples -- this confirms lexical and removes the 'no explicit sentence' weakness; Saramandu & Nevaci 2020 is silent on placement. (4) The modern monographs (Atanasov 1990, 2002) are not yet obtained and print-only, but Narumov's sketch derives from Atanasov's work, so a reclassify is unlikely. Suggested action: add Narumov 2001 p.675 as an explicit-rule supporting source (page-image grade)

sources.quote: «Ударение в М.я./д. силовое, свободное, может падать на любой слог: cāvé 'кофе', árburi 'дуб', dipárti 'далеко'.» [Stress in Megleno-Romanian is dynamic, free, may fall on any syllable: cāvé 'coffee' (final), árburi 'oak' (antepenult), dipárti 'far' (penult).] Same page also notes (after Atanasov) lengthening of stressed vowels and unstressed-vowel raising e>i, o>u, a>ă.

tone.quote: § 36. Vokale: a, e, i, o, u, ... e und sind mäßig geschlossen und finden sich wie auch ... auf dem ganzen Gebiete, nur mit dem Unterschiede, daß sie im Meglen im Gegensatze zu den übrigen Dialekten, wo sie kurz und halblang vorkommen, auch entschieden lang sein können, was dem Dialekte einen eigenartigen Charakter giebt.
tone.locator: p. 3, II. Teil, A. Lautlehre, §36 'Lautstand' (elided with '..')
tone.translation: §36. Vowels: a, e, i, o, u, [two further symbols]. e and [o] are moderately close and, like [i, u], occur over the whole area, with the one difference that in Meglen, in contrast to the other dialects, where they are short and half-long, they can also be decidedly long, which gives the dialect a peculiar character.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: No tone; vowel length noted as characteristic (long stressed vowels).

tone.quote: Analizând cuvintele slave din listele lui Capidan (Megl. I 1925: 86 -94) ca şi cele din dicţionarul lui (Megl. III 1936), mai ales cele care au intrat în meglenoromână după separarea ei de dacoromână, constatăm că particularităţile lor esenţiale (accentul, închiderea vocalelor neaccentuate) sunt identice cu cele ale graiurilor macedonene care se vorbesc în imediata apropiere a satelor meglenoromâne din Meglen.
tone.locator: p. 85, paragraph beginning 'Elementele lexicale', after the four-degree vowel-system discussion
tone.translation: Analysing the Slavic words in Capidan's lists (Megl. I 1925: 86-94) and in his dictionary (Megl. III 1936), especially those that entered Megleno-Romanian after its separation from Daco-Romanian, we find that their essential features (the accent, the closing of unstressed vowels) are identical to those of the Macedonian dialects spoken in the immediate vicinity of the Megleno-Romanian villages of Meglen.
tone.summary: No tone; stress language (accent of Slavic loans matches Macedonian dialects; unstressed-vowel closing).
